A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MR-GPTQ and QuTLASS study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization simulations, Llama and Qwen accuracy evaluations, component ablations, repeated-run results, and GPU performance measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of integer microscaling formats, scale fitting, additional precision baselines, and inference regimes.

M1.justification: The original MR-GPTQ components remain, but Appendix H introduces MXFP4†, which fits the scale grid to the observed logarithmic data range and changes the quantization mapping. Section 5 and Appendix D also introduce NVINT4 and MXINT4 using a symmetric integer grid with microscaling. These substantially extend the proposed quantization designs.

E1.justification: The FineWeb calibration data, Tülu 3 training data, Llama/Qwen models, standard evaluation tasks, and Platinum benchmark coverage are retained. The additions concern quantization formats and inference configurations rather than new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 adds INT8 and FP8 RTN/GPTQ comparisons and NVINT4/MXINT4 alternatives in Table 1 and Appendix B. Figure 12 adds FP8 and weight-only NVFP4 performance comparators. The Platinum comparison also gains the MXFP4 identity-transform, MinMax-scale, default-order variant, previously missing from its reported results.

E3.justification: The new B200 evaluation extends end-to-end testing to batch size 1 and reports latency and throughput across inference regimes. Section 5 also changes the stated RTN+HT rotation size from format-specific 16/32 in v1 to 32 in v3; unchanged corresponding scores do not establish that this experiment was rerun. Existing calibration budgets and principal accuracy metrics remain.

E4.justification: New analyses test Hadamard transforms and outlier preservation for integer microscaling formats, compare fitted versus original MXFP scales, and investigate performance across memory-bound and larger-batch inference. These add substantive diagnostic questions beyond the retained scale-format and transform ablations. The Platinum analysis is relocated and updated, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed evaluations, recovery means and standard deviations, distribution plots, and variance-based highlighting. Filling the missing Platinum result and revising plotted values extend existing reporting practices; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or explicit increase in runs is reported.

E6.justification: Most original FP4 table values remain unchanged, but v3 adds extensive format, scale-fitting, and performance results. Examples include 97.12% recovery for NVINT4 MR-GPTQ in Table 1 and 94.3% for Llama-8B MXFP4† RTN in Table 11. Platinum heatmaps revise Had128-MSE-ActOrder recovery from 91.9% to 92.1%, while Table 12 fills the missing identity/MinMax/default-order result with 84.85% and standard deviation 1.95. These are additions and reported revisions, not a general same-setting improvement of the original method.

T1.justification: Appendix D defines the integer microscaling grids, and Appendix H adds mathematical expressions for logarithmic scale fitting and scale multiplication with a shared exponent parameter. The original error bounds, assumptions, and supplied proofs remain substantively unchanged, including the material moved from Appendix D to Appendix E.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims about FP4 limitations, MR-GPTQ accuracy recovery, and low-overhead QuTLASS acceleration. The headline speedups and stated contributions remain the same; the added experiments do not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix G adds an important applicability boundary: the kernels offer little or no advantage at small batch sizes, where memory-bound inference favors weight-only quantization. Appendices D and H add interpretations favoring rotated NVINT4 and range-fitted scales, together with a shared-exponent requirement for efficient arithmetic. These materially expand the paper's guidance on when different designs are useful.

D1.justification: The new Reproducibility Statement adds a link to a collection of MR-GPTQ model checkpoints. The FP-Quant and QuTLASS code links were already present in v1; their relocation is not a new code release. Existing calibration and hardware disclosures are largely retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al.'s study of integer versus floating-point quantization and explicitly relates its integer-format findings to that work. It also adds Lee et al.'s block-wise PTQ and distillation-based QAT reference to the QAT discussion. The broader related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 condenses experimental subsections and bullet lists, moves the Platinum discussion to Appendix I, and introduces a separate Reproducibility Statement. Author presentation and conference headers also change. Most existing explanatory prose is retained, so this is a limited reorganization rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adds a format schematic, integer-error and inference-regime plots, and a scale-fitting table. It substantially expands accuracy tables, redesigns the aggregate recovery display, splits the original kernel-performance figure, and relocates the Platinum displays. These are substantial changes to the visual presentation beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added precision comparators and explicit small-batch limitation improve the paper's practical assessment, and the new format analyses broaden its explanatory value. However, reporting problems limit the gain: NVINT4/GPTQ Llama-3B recovery is 73.44% in Table 4 but 92.5% in Table 10, and Appendix H's Equation 2 does not reproduce its stated range mapping as printed. With the original central evidence largely unchanged, these additions support a limited net improvement.
